claims.text: A roughly 100 nm ZrN layer can be deposited between elemental Cr and Zircaloy as an interfacial diffusion barrier.
The ZrN interlayer can be deposited by a PVD or CVD process below 500°C.
Directly deposited Cr coatings on Zircaloy are prone to premature failure from elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The proposed ZrN layer will remain continuous at the Cr–Zircaloy interface under the stated exposures.
ZrN is chemically inert under the stated subcritical-water and high-temperature-steam conditions.
A roughly 100 nm ZrN layer is thermally stable during exposures up to approximately 1100–1200°C.
ZrN has sufficiently low relevant atomic diffusivity to impede migration between Cr and Zircaloy.
The ZrN interlayer will suppress Cr–Zr atomic migration at the coating–substrate interface.
Suppressing Cr–Zr migration will prevent or reduce formation of an interdiffusion zone.
Cr–Zr interdiffusion zones compromise coating adhesion.
Cr–Zr interdiffusion zones compromise the protective functionality of the Cr coating.
Relative to a direct Cr-on-Zircaloy baseline, the ZrN-bearing samples will develop markedly thinner interdiffusion zones.
Relative to the baseline, the ZrN-bearing samples will exhibit delayed coating failure.
The ZrN barrier will preserve effective oxidation resistance during long-term exposure to subcritical water at approximately 300–400°C.
The ZrN barrier will preserve effective oxidation resistance during steam exposure at approximately 1100–1200°C for a few minutes.
Long-term adhesion and continuity of the ultrathin ZrN barrier under cyclic thermal conditions are uncertain.
Statistical equivalence between barrier and baseline samples in interdiffusion-zone thickness, adhesion strength, or oxidation resistance under the specified tests would falsify the hypothesis.
